description: Our team is tackling the 'Planet X and SPHEREx' challenge by building an interactive web tool to visualize our changing universe. We are transforming SPHEREx’s massive near-infrared sky survey data into an intuitive, public-facing platform. By making it easy to track shifting celestial objects like comets, asteroids, and the hypothetical Planet X over time, we aim to democratize astronomy and empower anyone to join the cosmic hunt!

The NASA SPHEREx 102-Hyperspectral Channel Engine (LVF Bands D1–D6)

  • What it does: Instead of standard RGB images, the app processes hyperspectral data across 102 distinct channels spanning 0.75 to 5.00 μm0.75\text{ to }5.00\ \mu\text{m}0.75 to 5.00 μm across six Linear Variable Filter (LVF) detector arrays (D1–D6).
  • Bridging the Gap: It exposes professional-grade NASA survey data to students and citizens, allowing them to inspect exact monochromatic wavelengths, track molecular absorption troughs, and analyze thermal emission peaks just like a working astrophysicist.

2. Multi-Epoch Blink Comparator & Calibrated Astrometry

  • What it does: Users can "blink" between multiple chronological observation epochs to spot changes, track proper motion, and measure pixel shifts. It features automated FWHM (Full Width at Half Maximum) morphology checks, background noise subtraction, and WCS coordinate tracking.
  • Bridging the Gap: It gamifies and simplifies professional astrometric pipelines, enabling citizens and students to distinguish between stationary deep-space objects (stars, galaxies, quasars, supernovae) and moving Solar System transients (asteroids, comets) using real-world kinematic rules.

3. Parameter-Driven 3D Appearance & Color System

  • What it does: Rather than relying on static 3D files, the application links local .glb models (ast.glb, comet.glb, brown_dwarf.glb, galaxy.glb, etc.) to a real-time shader and PBR material engine. It translates recorded parameters—such as effective temperature (TeffT_{\text{eff}}Teff​), flux, angular velocity, and FWHM—into live visual transformations (e.g., morphing brown dwarf cloud decks between L1 golden-orange, T1 crimson-red, and T7 indigo-magenta subtypes based on methane absorption).
  • Bridging the Gap: It transforms abstract numerical telemetry and spectroscopy graphs into intuitive, physically accurate 3D visual representations, making complex physical properties instantly understandable for learners and researchers.

4. Interactive Citizen Science Quiz Lab & Live Database Verification

  • What it does: A structured, two-stage scientific workflow where users evaluate kinematics (speed), morphology (FWHM/halo ratio), and photometry before making a structured deduction. Once submitted, the app cross-references live professional catalogs (NASA JPL SBDB, IMCCE SkyBoT, CDS SIMBAD, NED, and ATNF Pulsar Catalogs) and awards citizen science points.
  • Bridging the Gap: It creates a direct feedback loop between education and professional research, turning citizens into active contributors who can verify real discoveries and log them into a persistent SQLite database.

5. NASA JPL-Style Spectrophotometry & Photometry Graphs with Shaded Elemental Bands

  • What it does: Generates interactive 102-channel spectral curves featuring shaded vertical columns that highlight molecular and elemental signatures (H2O\text{H}_2\text{O}H2​O, CH4\text{CH}_4CH4​, CO2\text{CO}_2CO2​, CO\text{CO}CO, silicates, and PAHs).
  • Bridging the Gap: It bridges raw data and theoretical understanding by visually explaining why an object is classified a certain way (e.g., matching the 3.3 μm methane dropout or the 4.26 μm CO2\text{CO}_2CO2​ cometary outgassing spike), serving as an educational powerhouse for students and an analytical quick-reference for researchers.
